useCases.title: Run Claude Code through AnyRouter
useCases.summary: Run Claude Code through AnyRouter with one command
useCases.hook: Install the anyr CLI, then anyr claude — it injects the base URL, key, and model. Env vars are the fallback if you already run claude yourself.
useCases.problem: Claude Code talks to Anthropic by default. To use other models, share billing across tools, or keep an audit log, you need a custom base URL without rewriting how the CLI works.
steps: Install the anyr CLI with the curl | bash one-liner (native binary, no npm).
Run anyr claude. First run signs you in or pastes an sk-ar- key; later runs reuse ~/.anyrouter/config.yaml.
Pin a catalog model when you want one (anyr claude --model anyrouter/auto). Env vars remain the manual fallback.

snippets.code:
curl -fsSL https://anyrouter.dev/setup.sh | bash
anyr claude
snippets.title: anyr CLI

snippets.code:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://anyrouter.dev/api"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$ANYROUTER_API_KEY"
claude
snippets.title: Env wrapper

diagram.label: Claude Code sends requests to AnyRouter, which forwards them to the model you picked.

useCases.title: Grok Bot + Herdr + Anyr CLI coding loop

useCases.hook: A live coding agent on a repo checkout: Grok Bot assigns the goal, Herdr shows the box, and the anyr CLI launches Claude Code through AnyRouter.
useCases.problem: Cursor cloud on-demand can be exhausted or blocked. You still need a live terminal you can attach, a fleet manager to assign goals, and a way to run Claude Code against catalog models.
steps: Install the anyr CLI if needed, then open a Herdr space on the repo checkout at the branch tip.
Launch anyr claude in that space with --yolo so it injects the base URL, key, and model.
Paste the goal into Grok Bot and let it drive the agent; squash-merge the PR and deploy from local.

useCases.title: Run Hermes Agent on AnyRouter
useCases.summary: Install the AnyRouter plugin and pick a model
useCases.hook: Install the AnyRouter provider plugin, add one key, and Hermes lists only the models that can call tools.
useCases.problem: Hermes Agent runs long tool loops, and a single upstream model means you eat that provider's outages and rate limits. Picking a model that cannot call tools breaks the loop.
steps: Install the plugin with hermes plugins install anyrouter, then check it with hermes plugins list.
Add the key to ~/.hermes/.env as ANYROUTER_API_KEY=sk-.... Get one at anyrouter.dev; the same key also works against the OpenAI-compatible endpoint anyrouter.dev/api/v1.

Pick a model: run hermes model and choose anyrouter, or launch with hermes --provider anyrouter -m anyrouter/hermes. anyrouter/hermes auto-routes across the top tool-calling models with fallback, a good default for agentic work.

snippets.code:
hermes plugins install anyrouter
hermes plugins list
snippets.title: Install the plugin

snippets.code: ANYROUTER_API_KEY=sk-...
snippets.title: ~/.hermes/.env

snippets.code: hermes --provider anyrouter -m anyrouter/hermes
snippets.title: Run Hermes on AnyRouter

useCases.title: OpenRouter free models, with fallback to another free model
useCases.summary: Free models that fall back to another free model
useCases.hook: Call a :free model by id. If its routes are rate limited or down, AnyRouter answers through anyrouter/free instead, with a different free model, and tells you which one.
useCases.problem: A free model on one route runs out at busy hours, and a script that retries the same route keeps failing. You want a different free model to answer without writing the retry yourself.
steps: Call a :free model id with your AnyRouter key, as in the curl below. No provider key is needed and no credits are used.
Check the model field in the response, and the X-AnyRouter-Fallback header. When the header reads anyrouter/free, a different free model answered.

snippets.code:
curl -si https://anyrouter.dev/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANYROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "google/gemma-4-31b:free",
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence." }]
  }' | grep -i -e x-anyrouter-fallback -e '"model"'
snippets.title: curl · which model answered

diagram.label: Your app calls AnyRouter with a :free model. If that model's routes are rate limited, AnyRouter answers with a different free model through anyrouter/free.

notes: The fallback is a different model. Pin another model, or check the header, if you need that exact one.
limits: The fallback answers with a different free model. It does not raise OpenRouter's or any provider's limit.
Free requests allow 2400 a minute per API key and have no daily cap.
When every free route is busy, the request fails and you retry later.

useCases.title: OpenRouter free models in OpenCode and Cline
useCases.summary: One OpenAI-compatible URL for Cline, OpenCode and more
useCases.hook: Any tool with an OpenAI-compatible provider can use free models through one base URL. Set the key and a :free model id, and the tool needs no other setup.
useCases.problem: Each editor tool wants its own provider, key and model list. Free models change often, so the setup you copied last month points at a model that is gone.

In the tool, add an OpenAI-compatible provider with the base URL and your key, and set the model to a :free id such as google/gemma-4-31b:free.
Prefer a model that AnyRouter picks for you? Use anyrouter/free instead. If a :free model has no route left, AnyRouter answers through anyrouter/free.

useCases.title: NVIDIA NIM models through one endpoint
useCases.summary: Call NVIDIA models with an AnyRouter key
useCases.hook: Call Nemotron and other NVIDIA models with your AnyRouter key. Some run on a free shared route. You can also pin your own NVIDIA key to them.
useCases.problem: NVIDIA's endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, but it is one more key, one more base URL and one more rate limit to track next to your other providers.
steps: Pick a model on the NVIDIA page of the catalog. Models marked Free run on the shared route.
Call it with your AnyRouter key, as in the curl below.

Optional: get a key at build.nvidia.com (it starts with nvapi-), add it under Dashboard → BYOK → NVIDIA NIM, and turn on Always use → Strict. Requests for these models then use only your key, and if it fails the request fails.

snippets.code:
curl https://anyrouter.dev/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANYROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b",
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence." }]
  }'
snippets.title: curl · nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b

diagram.label: Your app calls AnyRouter, which sends the request to an NVIDIA NIM model, on the shared free route or on your own NVIDIA key.

limits: NVIDIA's free developer tier allows about 40 requests a minute per key and is meant for development and testing (see docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/api-quickstart).
The shared free route is shared by every user, so at busy hours a request can fail.
With your own key pinned in Strict mode, the limit and any billing are NVIDIA's, on your account. AnyRouter adds no markup.
Which NVIDIA models are free can change. The catalog page shows the current price.

useCases.title: Gemini models in Claude Code
useCases.summary: Pick a Gemini model inside Claude Code
useCases.hook: Claude Code talks to the Messages API, and AnyRouter translates it for any catalog model. Save a Google key, then choose a Gemini model with --model.
useCases.problem: You like Claude Code's loop but want to try Gemini on the same repo, without switching to another tool or editing its config by hand.
steps: Create a key in Google AI Studio, then add it under Dashboard → BYOK → Google AI Studio.
Install the anyr CLI and run anyr claude with a Gemini model. A concrete --model also sets Claude Code's haiku, sonnet, opus and subagent models, so background tasks use Gemini too.
Prefer plain env vars? Point ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at https://anyrouter.dev/api and pass the same model to claude.

snippets.code:
curl -fsSL https://anyrouter.dev/setup.sh | bash
anyr claude --model google/gemini-2.5-pro
snippets.title: anyr CLI

snippets.code:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://anyrouter.dev/api"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$ANYROUTER_API_KEY"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="google/gemini-2.5-pro"
claude --model google/gemini-2.5-pro
snippets.title: Env wrapper

diagram.label: Claude Code sends Messages API requests to AnyRouter. AnyRouter translates them and calls a Gemini model on your Google key.

limits: Gemini routes run on keys you add, so Google's limits and billing apply to your account.
Claude Code is built around Claude. Gemini models vary in how well they handle tool calls and long edits.
With plain env vars, set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL too, or Claude Code's small background tasks still call a Claude model.
Features that exist only on Anthropic's API, such as its prompt cache, do not apply on a Gemini route.

useCases.title: Several provider keys behind Claude Code
useCases.summary: Add more than one provider key and fail over
useCases.hook: Save keys for more than one provider. Claude Code keeps one URL, and AnyRouter tries the next provider when one fails.
useCases.problem: One revoked, paused or capped key stops Claude Code mid-task. Swapping keys in your shell by hand loses the session.
steps: Add a key for one provider under Dashboard → BYOK, then add a key for a second provider, such as OpenRouter.
On each provider card, keep the Fallback strategy. Round Robin and Weighted spread requests across a provider's keys instead.
Run anyr claude. anyrouter/coding picks from every model your saved keys can reach and moves on if a provider is busy.

snippets.code:
curl -fsSL https://anyrouter.dev/setup.sh | bash
anyr claude --model anyrouter/coding
snippets.title: anyr CLI

diagram.label: Claude Code calls AnyRouter. AnyRouter tries your first provider. If it fails or is rate limited, AnyRouter tries your second provider.

limits: Keys for one provider should come from one account you own. A second key there is redundancy against a revoked key, not more rate limit.
Fallback moves to the next key on a rate limit or provider error. If every key fails, the provider's error comes back.
A key that fails repeatedly is marked unhealthy and skipped until it recovers.

Call model anyrouter/free for the subsidized free chain, or anyrouter/auto for paid models that are healthy right now.
Read the model pages and the free-tier docs for failover behavior.

useCases.title: Bring your own Anthropic key
useCases.summary: Use your own Anthropic plan through one AnyRouter endpoint
useCases.hook: Add your sk-ant key once. Claude models then run on your Anthropic plan and limits, billing stays on your Anthropic account, and one AnyRouter endpoint can fall back to other models.
useCases.problem: You already pay Anthropic, and your plan has its own limits and billing. Add that key to AnyRouter and keep one endpoint and one API for every tool, with other models ready if Claude is busy or you hit a limit.
steps: Open Dashboard → BYOK → Add key.
Pick Anthropic and paste your sk-ant-… key.
Press Test key. It checks the key and the models you picked.
Save the key.
Call anthropic/claude-… models with your AnyRouter key, from curl or from Claude Code with anyr claude.

snippets.code:
curl https://anyrouter.dev/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANYROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence." }]
  }'
snippets.title: curl · anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6

snippets.code:
curl -fsSL https://anyrouter.dev/setup.sh | bash
anyr claude --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
snippets.title: Claude Code · anyr claude

notes: Your key is encrypted at rest and used only to route your own requests.
Test key makes a tiny call to Anthropic for each model you picked. Nothing is saved until you press Add key.
A key that has not passed a test is saved paused and does not route.
To turn a key off, open the Anthropic key list on the BYOK page and switch the key to Off. Traffic moves to your other keys or to AnyRouter credits.
To remove a key, open the same list and use the trash icon. The key is deleted for good.

useCases.title: Let users sign in with their AnyRouter account
useCases.summary: Give your app a temporary inference-only key
useCases.hook: Your app gets a temporary inference-only key. Their balance pays. You never store a raw provider secret.
useCases.problem: Shipping your own LLM keys means you eat every user's bill. Asking them to paste an OpenAI key is a bad secret-handling story.
steps: Register your app and implement the OAuth 2.1 + PKCE consent flow.
Exchange the code for a short-lived sk-ar-v1 key scoped to that user.
Call models on their behalf — start with anyrouter/free or anyrouter/auto.

snippets.code: https://anyrouter.dev/oauth/consent
snippets.title: Consent endpoint

useCases.title: Manage models and keys from any MCP client
useCases.summary: One MCP endpoint for every client
useCases.hook: One Streamable HTTP endpoint. Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode call your workspace as tools.
useCases.problem: Checking credits, listing models, or rotating a key means leaving the editor. MCP puts those tools next to the agent.
steps: Point the MCP client at https://anyrouter.dev/api/v1/mcp.
Complete OAuth when the client prompts.
Use the landing page recipes for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode.

snippets.code: https://anyrouter.dev/api/v1/mcp
snippets.title: MCP endpoint

useCases.title: Give agents MCP tools without per-client sprawl
useCases.summary: Connect agents to AnyRouter over MCP
useCases.hook: Understand what an MCP server is, then connect agents to AnyRouter instead of pasting a new config into every app.
useCases.problem: Every new MCP server is another token and another JSON blob copied into Claude Desktop, Cursor, and your own agents.
steps: Read how MCP servers expose tools over one JSON-RPC transport.
Point clients at AnyRouter's MCP endpoint instead of N server URLs.
Keep model calls on anyrouter/auto so tool-using agents have a healthy default.
